Art. 21(2)(a).title: Policies on risk analysis and information system security
Art. 21(2)(a).description: Establishment and implementation of policies on risk analysis and information system security.

Art. 21(2)(b).title: Incident handling
Art. 21(2)(b).description: Policies and procedures for incident handling (prevention, detection and response).

Art. 21(2)(c).title: Business continuity and crisis management
Art. 21(2)(c).description: Measures for business continuity, such as backup management and disaster recovery, and crisis management.

Art. 21(2)(d).title: Supply chain security
Art. 21(2)(d).description: Supply chain security, including security-related aspects concerning the relationships between each entity and its direct suppliers or service providers.

Art. 21(2)(e).title: Security in acquisition, development and maintenance
Art. 21(2)(e).description: Security in network and information systems acquisition, development and maintenance, including vulnerability handling and disclosure.

Art. 21(2)(f).title: Assessing the effectiveness of risk-management measures
Art. 21(2)(f).description: Policies and procedures to assess the effectiveness of cybersecurity risk-management measures.

Art. 21(2)(g).title: Cyber hygiene and training
Art. 21(2)(g).description: Basic cyber hygiene practices and cybersecurity training.

Art. 21(2)(h).title: Use of cryptography and encryption
Art. 21(2)(h).description: Policies and procedures regarding the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption.

Art. 21(2)(i).title: Human resources security, access control and asset management
Art. 21(2)(i).description: Human resources security, access control policies and asset management.

Art. 21(2)(j).title: Multi-factor authentication and secured communications
Art. 21(2)(j).description: Use of multi-factor authentication or continuous authentication solutions, secured voice, video and text communications and secured emergency communication systems within the entity, where appropriate.

Art. 23(1).title: Early warning for significant incidents (within 24h)
Art. 23(1).description: Submission of an early warning without undue delay, and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of the significant incident.

Art. 23(2).title: Incident notification (within 72h)
Art. 23(2).description: Submission of an incident notification without undue delay, and in any event within 72 hours of becoming aware of the significant incident.

Art. 23(4).title: Final report (no later than one month after notification)
Art. 23(4).description: Submission of a final report no later than one month after the submission of the incident notification.

profile.title: Affectedness profile
profile.modalIntro: The classification decides which criteria of the catalogue apply at all. It is a management decision carrying liability and is recorded in the audit log.
profile.notePlaceholder: What does the classification follow from? Thresholds, sector, customer contracts …
profile.unknownHint: Not classified yet — until then the full catalogue applies as for an essential entity. That is the safe assumption, but it is no substitute for an assessment.
profile.excluded: {{count}} of {{total}} criteria do not apply to this profile and are excluded from the rate.
profile.syncHint: Adds criteria introduced in a newer version. Existing entries are left untouched.

essential.label: Essential entity (Annex I)
essential.description: Energy, transport, banking, financial markets, health, drinking and waste water, digital infrastructure, ICT services, space, public administration. Full catalogue, proactive supervision.

important.label: Important entity (Annex II)
important.description: Postal and courier, waste, chemicals, food, manufacturing, digital providers, research. Same duties under Art. 21 and 23, ex-post supervision.

indirect.label: Indirectly affected only (supply chain)
indirect.description: Not in scope itself, but a supplier or service provider to an entity that is. No duties towards the authority; requirements arrive contractually via Art. 21(2)(d).

unknown.label: Not classified yet
unknown.description: Until classified, the rate is computed as for an essential entity — better to check too much than to miss a duty you have.

empty.title: Question catalogue not loaded yet
empty.description: 37 questions along NIS2 Articles 20, 21 and 23, each on two axes: is the measure in place, and can we prove it? From that come the fulfilment rate, a maturity level per topic, and a gap list.

selfCheck.syncedNone: The question catalogue is already complete.
selfCheck.taskCreated: Task created and linked to the question.
selfCheck.noGaps: No gaps — everything answered is in place and evidenced.
selfCheck.noGapsUnanswered: No question answered yet. Gaps appear as the questionnaire is filled in.
selfCheck.coverageHint: Coverage per NIS2 element: on the left what the questionnaire says, on the right what the criteria catalogue tracks. An element with no question is unchecked — not fulfilled.

import.title: Import an answer set
import.intro: One line per question: identifier, implementation, evidence, optionally the evidence source. Separator semicolon, tab or comma; "Ja", "Teilweise" and "Nein" are recognised alongside the English words. A header line is skipped.

scoring.title: Scoring model
scoring.intro: There is no generally agreed way to turn "partly implemented" into a percentage. These settings fix one — for the criteria catalogue and the questionnaire alike. Every change is written to the audit log, so a rate stays explainable afterwards.
scoring.weightHint: Without the measure there is nothing to document — but it still has to be documented (Art. 21(1)).
scoring.partlyHint: Applies on both axes, and to "in progress" in the criteria catalogue.
scoring.gate: Not implemented scores 0, even with evidence
scoring.gateHint: Evidence for something that does not exist is a contradiction. Switchable, in case a framework sees it differently.
scoring.maturityHint: Lower bounds. Values out of order are sorted descending on save — otherwise a higher rate would yield a lower maturity.
scoring.error: The scoring model could not be saved.

subCriteria.progressHint: Derived from the sub-criteria. The parent carries the legal reference; the sub-items are what gets counted.
